transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Well, hello doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for fitting me in. I know I’m probably a bit older than the usual folks you see for this sort
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I know I'm getting up there in years, but my mind isn't playing tricks on me in that way! My hearing isn't quite what it used to be, to be perfectly honest with you—just the other day I thought I heard the mail carrier on the porch and I went all the way to the front door, which is quite a walk from my sitting room, and it turned out to just be the wind knocking a loose branch against the gutters. We really need to get those gutters cleaned out, actually, before the weather turns. But as far as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't really there, like... well, like
Have you been having problems with your memory?
Oh, heavens no. No, my memory is actually quite sharp, thank goodness. I mean, well, sure, I might forget why I walked into a room every now and then, or
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Oh, no, no. I really haven't. I know sometimes people my age get a bit down, what with getting older and the aches and pains and all that, but
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
Oh, no, not really. I've never been much of a worrier, to tell you the truth. Now, my sister, she's a completely different story—she watches the
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or high for several days?

Oh, goodness, no. I mean, I certainly have days where I get a little burst of energy to, say, clean out the hall closet—you know how that goes, you just wake up and decide today is the day the winter coats finally need sorting out. But I wouldn't ever call it feeling "high" or anything like that for days on end. Goodness, at my age, if I have just one busy afternoon where I'm running around doing errands or maybe pulling a few weeds out by the mailbox, I am quite ready for a nice cup
Did something stressful happen in your life shortly before these symptoms began?
Oh, no, I wouldn't say so at all. My life is actually very quiet these days. I mean, since I stopped working and the kids are all grown up and out of the house
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Oh, no, I've always been quite a good sleeper, actually. I mean, occasionally I might wake up to use the restroom, which is just what happens when you get to be my age, but I go right back to sleep. I usually head up to bed around 10 o'clock after I finish watching my evening programs—I like to watch those little British mysteries, they're so charming, though sometimes the accents are a bit thick and I have to turn the volume up just a smidge so I don't miss the clues. But really, once my head hits the pillow, I am out like a light. I did buy a new mattress pad a few months ago, one of those memory foam ones, because my friend Martha swore by hers, and I have to say, it really does cradle your back nicely. It took a little getting used to, of course, because it had this strange factory smell that took days to air out, I had to leave the windows
What symptom has been bothering you the most lately?

Well, it's just this feeling that I can't seem to just sit still and be. I feel like I'm always up and moving, just constantly on the go, even when I have absolutely nothing on the calendar. Like yesterday, for instance, it was a perfectly quiet Tuesday, and I sat down with my tea to look over the garden club roster—I'm the secretary this year, you know, and keeping track of everyone's dues is quite the task, especially since Mrs. Higgins insists on paying with a check that always seems to arrive late. But before I even finished checking off the names, I was suddenly up and digging through my knitting bag because I remembered I needed to check the dye lot on the blue yarn for my grandson's sweater. And then, while I was doing that, I saw the travel brochures for that river cruise Martha and I were talking about, and the next thing I knew, I was at the dining room table sorting through those. It's just bouncing from one thing to the next, to the next, before I've really finished any one of them. It's exhausting, frankly, because at the end of the day, I look around and the roster isn't updated, the sweater isn't knitted, and the trip isn't booked, but I feel like I've been running a marathon in my own living room! I just can't seem to settle my mind or my body down to just do one simple thing at a time, and it's really starting to wear me out.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still and jumping from one thing to another when you were a child?

Oh, my goodness, yes. It's funny you should ask that, because I was just thinking about my old report cards the other day. I was cleaning out the attic—well, I say cleaning, but really I just moved three boxes from one side of the room to the other before I got distracted by an old photo album. But anyway, I found this little stack of report cards from when I was at Lincoln Elementary. And, oh, it was the same story every single year. My teachers, especially Mrs. Gable in the third grade—she was a lovely woman, wore these beautiful floral dresses and always smelled like lavender—she told my mother, "She's bright, she really is, but she's just so scattered." And it was true! I was always losing my spelling lists, or my homework would just vanish into thin air between the kitchen table and my desk at school. And the wiggling! Oh, I could never just sit in my chair. I'd be swinging my legs, or tapping my pencil, or turning around to talk to whoever was behind me—usually Tommy Miller, who was always getting into trouble himself. I'd just blurt things out before raising my hand, and I'd be up and out of my seat before I even finished my arithmetic worksheet. My mother used to say I had ants in my pants, and I suppose she was right. It's just strange to think that at seventy years old, I'm still feeling exactly the same way I did when I was eight, just buzzing around like a bee caught in a jar, never quite landing on any one flower for long enough...
